what: Banco Santander Brasil is the Brazilian arm of the Spanish bank Santander and one of the largest private banks in Brazil. It offers current accounts, cards, car loans, mortgages and corporate banking.
customers: Brazilian households, small businesses and corporations.
money: deposits, cards, personal and car loans
corporate lending, trade finance and treasury
moat: Scale in a concentrated Brazilian banking market, with the backing and funding access of a large European parent.
risks: Brazilian interest rates and unemployment drive credit losses
Car lending, where it is strong, is one of the most loss-prone categories
Digital banks have taken share in payments and cards
The parent's priorities can override minority shareholders'
opportunities: Analysts see about 33% upside from current levels
Brazilian credit penetration is still low relative to developed markets
watch: The non-performing loan ratio and return on equity.
